primary_finding: Prior inpatient utilization is the strongest individual predictive dependency in the locked model.
principal_caveat: Permutation importance measures predictive dependence, not causal effect.

primary_finding: Prior utilization is the dominant conceptual feature family, followed by encounter characteristics, diagnosis family, and clinical complexity.
principal_caveat: Grouped permutation effects are not additive across correlated feature families.

primary_finding: Estimated readmission probability rises consistently across the supported range of prior inpatient encounters.
principal_caveat: Partial dependence describes fitted-model behavior and does not represent an intervention effect.

primary_finding: Primary diagnosis family provides the strongest engineered diagnosis-family signal and remains stable under stronger support requirements.
principal_caveat: No raw ICD-9 counterfactual model was fitted, so this does not establish superiority over raw diagnosis codes.

primary_finding: Length of stay shows meaningful nonlinear model behavior, with increasing estimates through the central range and a decline in the upper range.
principal_caveat: Upper-range behavior should not be interpreted as evidence that changing length of stay changes readmission risk.
